newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bonn envoys meet Hizbollah officials on Arad.
newsitem.headline: Bonn envoys meet Hizbollah officials on Arad.

text.p: German mediators met leaders of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah in Beirut on Friday to find a solution to the thorny issue of Arab captives held by Israel and Israeli soldiers missing in Lebanon, Lebanese officials said.

Hizbollah (Party of God) said the talks were conducted by its chief Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah and Germany's top security official Bernd Schmidbauer, who brokered a deal in July in which Israel exchanged two dead soldiers for the remains of 123 guerrillas.

"The talks dealt with the latest exchange operation and aim to continue the efforts to find a final solution to the issue of the prisoners and captives held in Khiam jail (in south Lebanon) and in Israeli jails," Hizbollah said in a statement.
The Khiam prison, where dozens of Lebanese guerrillas languish, is run by Israel's client South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia which also patrols an Israeli occupation buffer strip there.

Caretaker Interior Minister Michel al-Murr said after meeting Schimdbauer -- the intelligence services co-ordinator in Helmut Kohl's chancellery -- that the German team came to Beirut "to continue contacts to secure the release of the captives".
He said Schmidbauer's talks in Lebanon would focus mainly on missing Israeli airman Ron Arad, the only one believed alive among four Israeli soldiers missing in Lebanon since the 1980s.
"He will inform me of the results of his contacts after 48 hours," said Murr, adding that Schmidbauer had held contacts outside Lebanon as well.
Murr said Schmidbauer brought with him letters from two key prisoners in Israel: Hizbollah cleric Sheikh Abdel Karim Obeid, and Mustapha Dirani, head of the Islamist Faithful Resistance.
Both were seized from their homes in commando operations. Obeid was snatched from southern Lebanon in 1989 and Dirani from the Eastern Bekaa valley in 1994.

The Faithful Resistance is the faction that held Arad after his plane was shot down over south Lebanon in 1986. Israel has said in the past it believed Arad was held in Iran or by pro-Iranian supporters in Lebanon.
But Hizbollah has denied it holds Arad.

Nasrallah said a day after the July 21 Israel-Hizbollah swap that his group promised to seek information on the airman as the basis for continuing the German-brokered negotiations with Israel on a comprehensive prisoner exchange.
He said 112 captives remain at Khiam jail and some 70 in Israel. Hizbollah does not hold any Israeli or SLA captives, Nasrallah added.
Under the July swap deal, the SLA freed 45 captives from Khiam jail, while the fundamentalist group released 17 SLA captives.
